newsitem.title: USA: Snow, ice and cold bring winter misery to U.S.
newsitem.headline: Snow, ice and cold bring winter misery to U.S.

text.p: Much of the United States remained in winter's icy grip on Monday, with freezing conditions stretching from the Canadian border as far south as Florida and Mexico.
The Midwest, where two states have been declared disaster zones after fierce blizzards, remained bitterly cold, while deadly ice storms coated the South and heavy snow paralysed parts of the East.
More than two dozen deaths have been blamed on a blizzard that struck the Great Plains last week. Low temperatures broke records around the region and were only gradually warming up.

Among recent deaths were two women found frozen in their snowbound vehicles in North Dakota and six people who died in accidents on slippery highways in Texas and Louisiana. A 69-year-old Cincinnati man was killed when his clothes ignited as he stood too close to an electric stove to keep warm.

Another half-dozen motorists who became stranded for days by the blizzard survived thanks to blankets and stored food, officials in North Dakota said. Most highways were open again after crews cleared 20-foot-high (seven metre) snowdrifts.
President Bill Clinton has declared both North and South Dakota disaster areas after a series of winter storms.

Frigid weather kept city workers busy in Chicago rounding up the homeless and checking on heat problems. In St. Louis, extra commuter trains were added to shorten the waiting time for passengers standing on freezing platforms.

Chicago officials also had a new worry -- rising water levels in Lake Michigan, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers said. The level was a foot-and-a-half (46 cm) above average for this time of year because of heavy snow and rains.
In the winter of 1986, the lake was another two feet (60 cm) higher and storms carried ice-clogged waves into apartment buildings and streets along the Chicago shoreline.
Commerce was also affected by the cold on Monday as the Illinois River froze and stranded barges carrying grain and other commodities.

A desperate appeal for firewood by the Blackfeet tribe in Montana was answered when they received 20 truckloads from another reservation. But officials in Billings, Montana, kept a wary eye on the Yellowstone River, which threatened to flood because of ice jams downstream.
Colorado's Avalanche Information Centre said snow slide danger was "high" in the Rocky Mountains and recommended travelers postpone trips to the back country. Some mountain passes were closed.
As much as four inches (10 cm) of ice coated roads and snapped trees and power lines in Texas and Louisiana.
The coldest spot in the United State was Havre, Montana, at 34 degress below zero (minus 37 Celsius). Even Tallahassee, Florida, was at the freezing mark (zero Celsius).
